items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: We had trumpet, drum, sax, guitar, and piano. Drum, alto, sax, guitar, and piano.

ctx.x: What kind of piano player you called him? Huh? What did you call him?

A distillery. A distillery. A liquor. A distillery. Yeah, the stillery. Walking the stillery. Yeah. And Kemp, you remember little Kemp always called it. Oh yeah. He's a straight man, a circus man. He got to come off the circus with me. And old Willie, guitar player, keep his hair straight all the time. Yeah. What is that? Willie, what are they stillery? None of the stillery, none of them. But you know he made us some money, man. Oh sure now. He's singing all them numbers. The number was very popular there, you're…

Wasn't that, ain't that the time when I would bat up in Central? When y'all used to come over and visit us on Sunday when we was off? You remember when I was playing with Bat Brown at Suckoff's place? He used to play at Lewis. In Central, Lewis Suckoff.
